tldr: DeepSeek's retrained V4-Flash beat flagship V4 Pro on nine agent benchmarks in late July, released amid an intensifying China AI price war, before going fully open-source. Price-hike reports then built for a week ahead of a quiet "V4 Pro 0813" OpenRouter listing. DeepSeek confirmed V4 Pro as an official, price-hiked release — corroborated by four outlets — and shipped Harness, a free open-source Claude Code rival, the same day.
whats_new: A four-day-later ghacks.net recap (Aug 17) is the first outlet to cite benchmark gains behind DeepSeek's Aug 13 V4 Pro launch, alongside the already-known open-source Harness tool and price increases — still no official DeepSeek benchmark table or changelog.
why_it_matters: The price hike still changes the cost math against V4-Flash, and free open-source Harness lets you benchmark DeepSeek's agent stack against Claude Code directly; the newly cited benchmark gains remain unverified by an official DeepSeek changelog, so treat them as a claim to test, not a confirmed capability jump.

status.state: Out of preview · benchmark claims now surfacing
status.detail: DeepSeek's confirmed V4 Pro release exited preview citing agent-capability gains and shipped open-source Harness the same day, alongside sharply higher user pricing, then reached China's National Supercomputing Internet on Aug 15. As of Aug 17, ghacks.net is the first outlet to cite concrete benchmark gains behind the launch — still without an official DeepSeek benchmark table.

beats.headline: Retrained V4-Flash beats flagship V4 Pro on nine agent benchmarks
beats.summary: DeepSeek's cheaper Flash variant overtakes the company's own Pro model on agent-focused evaluations and ships as an official, fully open-source release — Nikkei Asia and Caixin both frame it as part of an intensifying China AI price war, and Semafor's Aug 3 follow-up repeats that framing — a lead a later hands-on finds only partly holds once Pro ships.

beats.headline: Price-hike reports build for over a week before DeepSeek confirms anything
beats.summary: Bloomberg, Investing.com, TechNode, The Next Web, China Daily, Semafor, Mashable, a CITIC Securities note, and regional coverage all flag a coming DeepSeek price increase for a week and a half before the official V4 Pro launch makes it real; the-decoder.com's Aug 12 comparison still finds DeepSeek beating Microsoft's MAI Code on price and performance as the hike looms.

beats.headline: A new "V4 Pro 0813" build appears on OpenRouter with no announcement
beats.summary: Simon Willison spots the refreshed Pro model listed API-only, with no DeepSeek announcement page to explain what changed.

beats.headline: Early hands-on says the refreshed Pro's multimodal capabilities meet expectations
beats.summary: The first outside impression of the new build focuses on multimodal quality rather than the agent-benchmark gap Flash had opened.

beats.headline: DeepSeek officially confirms the V4 Pro release
beats.summary: Four outlets — Lufkin Daily News, Reuters, The Information, and Global Times — independently report the Aug 12 OpenRouter build as a deliberate, confirmed release rather than a quiet leak; The Information frames it as a direct challenge to Kimi K3.

beats.headline: Official launch comes with sharply higher user prices
beats.summary: Nikkei Asia reports the confirmed release raises per-user pricing, without breaking out the new rate versus V4-Flash — the increase Chinese press and an analyst note had already flagged a week earlier.

beats.headline: DeepSeek open-sources Harness, a free agentic coding tool pitched against Claude Code
beats.summary: VentureBeat reports the release ships the same day as the pricier V4-Pro API, giving platform engineers a second reason to evaluate the drop.

beats.headline: V4 Pro exits preview status, DeepSeek cites agent-capability gains
beats.summary: The preview-exit framing points at agent gains but no benchmark numbers accompany the claim; state broadcaster CGTN and trade outlet Analytics India Magazine both repeat the same "agent capabilities" line over the next day, still without figures.

beats.headline: V4 Pro and Harness go live on China's National Supercomputing Internet
beats.summary: Global Times reports the official release now also runs on the state-backed supercomputing network, a distribution milestone with no new benchmark or pricing detail.

beats.headline: First outlet cites benchmark gains behind the V4 Pro launch
beats.summary: ghacks.net's four-days-later recap groups higher benchmarks, the open-source Harness tool, and the coming price increases into one story — the first mention of concrete benchmark gains since the Aug 13 launch, still without a DeepSeek-published table.

open_questions: Does V4 Pro's claimed "agent gains" reclaim the benchmark lead V4-Flash took in July, or does Flash remain the stronger agent option?
Does ghacks.net's Aug 17 benchmark claim cite an actual DeepSeek-published figure, or does it repeat the same unqualified "agent gains" framing as earlier state-media coverage?
How large is the new price increase, and does it still make Pro cheaper than V4-Flash per token for agent workloads?
Does DeepSeek publish benchmarks for the open-sourced Harness tool, and how does it compare to Claude Code on real agentic coding tasks?
Does the National Supercomputing Internet deployment change API access, pricing, or availability outside China, or is it a domestic-only distribution channel?
take_for_builders: Re-run your agent benchmark against the price-hiked V4 Pro 0813 build before trusting July's Flash-beats-Pro result, pull the new per-token pricing, and try DeepSeek's open-source Harness against your Claude Code workflows since it's free to test today.
